title: Choose the visual world for Eros Markets
question: The roll assigned the Depth Ladder: the logo's own grammar grown into the whole terminal. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Depth Ladder
options.lineage: the Eros mark: stacked ivory bars, one Signal bar for the mark price
options.thesis: The interface is the logo: price drawn as stacked bars, the mark price as one Signal bar that crosses chart, book and your position at the same height.
options.viewport: Market rail left; the chart owns the centre on Ink with the order book docked on the chart's own price axis; one Signal bar marks the mark across both; ticket right; position and margin strip below.
options.risk: If the bars become decoration instead of data, it reads as a logo pattern; every bar must be a real quantity.

raised.raise: Columns never move: every number is tabular and fixed-width, and a changed value flips digit by digit in 150 ms.
Signal is rationed to three jobs only: the mark price, the primary action, live risk.
A ruling discipline: every divider is a 1-device-pixel hairline, states are marks (filled, outlined, struck), no radius anywhere.
The lifecycle strip shows only the next deadline (T−12h30m, T−12h, T−1h, T) at large scale, re-signed after each one passes.
Unprinted Ink: the chart owns its field with no card chrome, frame or gradient around it.

options.label: Tote Board
options.thesis: Every market a live odds board: probabilities as big lit numerals that tick, the question as the race card.
options.viewport: Question and the YES probability at monumental scale over the chart, book and ticket beneath; markets as a board of numerals.
options.risk: Familiar betting-board register; can read as gambling rather than a leveraged derivatives venue.

options.label: Split-flap Concourse
options.thesis: Markets as departures: rows ranked by time to T, values cascading flap by flap.
options.viewport: Departure-board market list with countdowns to T.
options.case: Fuses: markets do have scheduled T; loses on clarity for the chart-led trading screen.
options.risk: Flap motion on every tick tires a trader.
options.kept: Columns never move; values flip per digit.

options.label: Monochrome Product Marketing
options.thesis: One neutral scale, one rare accent, every claim proved by an interface detail.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a marketing surface, not a working terminal.
options.risk: Ghost buttons and soft gradients break the sharp brand.

options.label: Centre-rail Reference Setting
options.thesis: A ruling engine draws every hairline and detent at one device pixel.
options.viewport: Two columns around a keyed rail.
options.case: Fuses poorly: an edition, not a trading screen.
options.kept: 1-device-pixel ruling, states as marks, no radius.

options.label: Terminal Yellow Wayfinding
options.thesis: Show only the next decision, monumental.
options.kept: Lifecycle strip shows only the next deadline.

options.label: Factory Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Matte black, one white plot owning the field.
options.case: Fuses partly: the chart-owns-the-field idea; coded labels hurt clarity.
options.risk: Coded labels are unreadable to newcomers.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark perp-exchange terminal executed impeccably, in Eros colours.
canonCard.viewport: Chart centre, book right, ticket far right, positions table below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other perp venues by design.
